clue.text: French capital responsible for Trojan development

explanation.surface: A city is credited with starting something in ancient Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trojan development' is the Trojan War, set going when the prince carried Helen off from Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: The French capital city bears this name, and the Trojan prince of that name abducted Helen, which started the Trojan War.

clue.text: Usual procedure is to include a deed in the cost

indicators.note: the cost word is made to hold another piece inside it

parts.note: the cost of something is its price
a deed is an act

explanation.surface: Customary practice is to fold a legal document into the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a deed' works as one phrase, and 'to include' signals the container; 'is' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Normal procedure is the established custom or habit, a common sense of the word.

clue.text: What one is likely to hear in a USSR organisation

definitions.text: What one is likely to hear

indicators.note: organising the letters of these words puts them in a new order

explanation.surface: A question about what language you'd hear inside a Soviet body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges IN A USSR.
explanation.definitionFit: The language spoken across the Soviet Union is what a listener there would mostly hear.

clue.text: A circus performer used to make an impression

explanation.surface: A big-top act tries hard to win over the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: The trained flippered mammal performs in circuses, and a stamp pressed into wax leaves an imprint.

clue.text: Writer who has to try before it's revised

parts.note: to essay something is to try it

indicators.note: revising the letters of these words rearranges them

explanation.surface: An author who makes an attempt before the piece is edited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is fodder spelt I-T-S; the apostrophe does not count, and 'revised' signals the reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who writes short prose compositions is a kind of author.

clue.text: Somehow so great a violent crime needs a shocking lot of cells

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of the words are jumbled into another order

parts.note: battery is the crime of physically attacking someone

explanation.surface: A big brutal crime somehow requires a horrifying number of prison cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges SO GREAT into STORAGE. The cells are electric cells, and 'shocking' refers to electric shocks, not to how bad the crime is.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank of electrical cells that holds charge for later use is an accumulator.

clue.text: Stake, not post

explanation.surface: A wager, but not one placed on a fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' is Latin for after, as in post-war; the Latin opposite is used for before, as in antenatal.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker player's opening stake goes in the pot, and the Latin word for before is the opposite of post, meaning after.

clue.text: One with a Latin disposition?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with a temperament from southern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' rearranges A LATIN into TALIAN, after I for 'One'. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of a Latin country could be called one with a Latin temperament.

clue.text: It upset the anti-clerical party

indicators.note: in a down entry something upset is turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Something annoyed the political party opposed to the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns IT into TI, followed by THE. As a whole, the church levy is just what would anger those against the clergy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenth of one's produce paid to support the church was a long-running grievance for opponents of the clergy.

clue.text: Clearly no good hiding from it under the bedclothes during a storm

definitions.text: Clearly no good hiding from it under the bedclothes during a storm

parts.words: Clearly no good hiding from it under the bedclothes during a storm
parts.note: pulling a bed cover over your head won't shut out the diffuse flashes that light up the whole sky in a thunderstorm, and the name itself includes a bed cover

explanation.surface: A frightened person in bed tries to hide from a thunderstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: Diffuse flashes that brighten clouds broadly during a thunderstorm, rather than a visible bolt.

clue.text: German town which gives curt answer to famous German composer

parts.note: ans is a short form of answer
Johann Sebastian Bach was a German baroque composer

explanation.surface: A place in Germany replies briefly to a celebrated musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bavarian town in Franconia, in the south of Germany.

clue.text: Survive all but the final ball of the innings

definitions.text: Survive all but the final ball of the innings

parts.words: Survive all but the final ball of the innings
parts.note: to last longer than everything else, and in cricket the batter dismissed at the very last ball is the one who is ...

explanation.surface: A cricket batter stays in until the very end of the innings.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an innings ends when batters are dismissed ('out'); one who goes at the final ball is the last out.
explanation.definitionFit: To live or endure longer than others is to survive them.

clue.text: Journey no experienced skipper should do

explanation.surface: Advice that a seasoned captain should avoid a certain voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'skipper' looks like a ship's captain but is someone skipping with a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A short excursion is a jaunt, and a practised rope-skipper never stumbles over the rope.

clue.text: Broken plate suggests a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: broken pieces are rearranged, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A smashed dish hints at a minor blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' rearranges PLATE. A 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the coloured leaves of a flower is part of something that blooms.

clue.text: Cheese-loving child?

parts.note: a tiny arachnid that infests cheese, and also an affectionate word for a small child

explanation.surface: A youngster with a fondness for cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny creature found in cheese shares its name with a word for a little child.

clue.text: Rommel giving hesitant exhortation to his troops

parts.note: er is the sound of a hesitant speaker
a general urges his soldiers to win

explanation.surface: The German field marshal haltingly urges on his army.
explanation.definitionFit: The German field marshal known as the Desert Fox had this as his first name.

clue.text: It is rare if you don't find it well done

definitions.text: It is rare if you don't find it well done

parts.words: It is rare if you don't find it well done
parts.note: rare and well done are opposite degrees of cooking a cut of beef, not measures of frequency or praise

explanation.surface: Something seems a rarity whenever it isn't done properly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of beef is ordered rare, medium or well done according to how long it is cooked.

clue.text: A nil tent charge ordered on in winter?

indicators.note: the letters of these words are ordered afresh into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: No charge for a tent is ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges A NIL TENT CHARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A home warming system is typically switched on during the cold months.

clue.text: The e insular type who confesses to defamation of character

parts.note: someone confessing speaks in the first person, saying I
slander is spoken defamation

explanation.surface: A person from a small island admits to bad-mouthing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: A confession would read 'I slander', giving I + SLANDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living on an island is literally insular, from the Latin for island.

clue.text: They have roles also in production but only till the boss returns

definitions.text: They have roles also in production but only till the boss returns

parts.words: They have roles also in production but only till the boss returns
parts.note: people who perform roles and run a production, but also deputies in charge only until the real head comes back

explanation.surface: Theatre people with parts who also run the show until the director is back.
explanation.definitionFit: Deputies temporarily in charge are standing in for an absent head.

clue.text: A nude in Connecticut might be employed in it

definitions.text: A nude in Connecticut might be employed in it

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: CT is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Connecticut
nude means bare

explanation.surface: An undressed performer in New England might work in a nightclub show.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also works as the definition: a nude performer might well appear in such a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub entertainment with music and dancing, sometimes risqué.

clue.text: How Mr Heath's friendly signature turned out?

parts.note: a letter between friends may close with 'ever', as in 'yours ever'
Ted was the first name used by Edward Heath, British prime minister 1970 to 1974

explanation.surface: Asking how a former prime minister's sign-off to friends turned out.
explanation.walkthrough: A friendly letter from Heath would be signed 'Ever, Ted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Turned inside out is the meaning of this term in anatomy and botany.

clue.text: Third power block

explanation.surface: A third force blocks something.
explanation.definitionFit: A number multiplied by itself twice is raised to the third power, and a solid with six square faces is a block.

clue.text: Desert mount Carmel when Rex deserts it

indicators.note: when a letter deserts a word it leaves it, so it is taken out

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A mountain in Israel loses its king and becomes a mount in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount Carmel' is a ridge in Israel; 'deserts' takes R out of CARMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The hump-backed animal is ridden across arid sands, so it is a desert steed.

clue.text: Say what condition

explanation.surface: Someone asks what shape things are in.
explanation.definitionFit: To state is to declare in words, and a state is a condition one is in.

clue.text: Spartan woman pronounced leader

indicators.note: pronounced points to a word that sounds the same when spoken

parts.note: the word leader said in a non-rhotic accent

explanation.surface: A woman of Sparta is declared to be in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: Said without the final R, as in southern British English, 'leader' sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the queen of Sparta was seduced by Zeus in swan form.

clue.text: Drug obtained from carbon monoxide and calcium

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula for carbon monoxide
Ca is the chemical symbol for calcium

explanation.surface: A narcotic made from two chemicals.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub whose leaves yield cocaine, and the leaves themselves, chewed as a stimulant.

clue.text: 150 supported by a north Scottish family

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece stands on top of the pieces below it

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: One hundred and fifty people backed by a northern Scottish family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supported by' places CL above A and N in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highland kinship group sharing a surname and chief.

clue.text: Polo in reverse suggested by an early broadcaster

parts.note: Marco Polo was the Venetian traveller

indicators.note: the word in is put in reverse, read backwards

explanation.surface: A Venetian explorer turned back, as proposed by a pioneer of radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Polo stands for the explorer's first name. 'in reverse' reads as a phrase, but 'in' is the fodder and 'reverse' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Guglielmo Marconi pioneered long-distance radio transmission.

clue.text: King in great spirits when told

parts.note: R is short for rex, Latin for king
elated means very happy

explanation.surface: A monarch is jubilant when he hears news.
explanation.definitionFit: A story that is recounted has been narrated.

clue.text: Grey, halt, and disposed to lack of energy

indicators.note: disposed here means arranged, so these letters are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A grey, lame figure inclined to sluggishness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges GREY and HALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Torpor or sluggishness is a want of vigour.

clue.text: Drain designed to reach the lowest point

indicators.note: designed means the letters are worked into a new layout

explanation.surface: A drain built to reach the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designed' rearranges DRAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomically, the point directly below an observer; figuratively, rock bottom.
